name: Construction Manager
description: Construction managers plan, price, schedule and deliver building projects — coordinating trades, controlling cost, enforcing code and safety, and answering for the programme. ⚠ A median of $114,990 with 9% growth, on a route with no licence gate at entry — compare architecture at $99,280 after an accredited degree, 3,740 supervised hours and a six-division exam. ⚠⚠⚠ And the finding that matters most in Florida: a construction degree is worth THREE YEARS of site experience toward a contractor licence under s. 489.111. This page covers three related roles, and two routes that look alike and end in different places.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠ Being a construction MANAGER requires no licence. Being a CONTRACTOR in Florida does, and the two are constantly confused. Under Chapter 489 the Construction Industry Licensing Board certifies contractors, and s. 489.111(2)(c) sets out the routes: a baccalaureate degree in ENGINEERING, ARCHITECTURE OR BUILDING CONSTRUCTION plus one year of proven experience — or at least four years of active experience as a worker in the trade with a minimum of one year as a foreman, with intermediate combinations trading college credits against foreman years. The statute measures a year as 2,000 person-hours. ⚠⚠⚠ Read that as a price: the degree substitutes for three years of site experience. Nowhere else on this site does a bachelor's convert so directly into a licence timeline. ⚠ Certification also requires passing the state contractor examinations — business and finance, contract administration and project management — and demonstrating financial responsibility, bonding and insurance, with fingerprinting. ⚠⚠ Note the limit: the education route names engineering, architecture and building construction. A BUSINESS degree is acceptable to employers hiring construction managers and does NOT satisfy this pathway, which leaves you on the four-year experience route.
bodyHtml:
Three roles, and the one that pays is the one with the degree

RoleSOC2025 medianJobsOutlook 2025–35Usual entry
Cost estimator13-1051$78,740226,400⚠ −3% declinebachelor's
First-line supervisor of construction trades47-1011$79,920921,6005–6% faster⚠ 27% certificate, 22% less than high school
Construction manager11-9021$114,990609,100✅ 9% much fasterbachelor's

⚠⚠⚠ The supervisor and the manager do overlapping work on the same site for a $35,070 difference, and the thing that separates them is a degree. The federal education data for first-line supervisors is striking: 27% postsecondary certificate, 22% less than a high school diploma, 21% high school — this is a job you reach by being good at a trade. The manager role lists a bachelor's and “work experience in a related occupation: none”.

⚠⚠ Two routes that look identical from outside

The BLS makes a distinction most people miss. Candidates with a high school diploma and several years of construction experience “may be more likely to work as self-employed general contractors than to be hired as construction managers”, and large firms prefer applicants who combine construction experience with a bachelor's degree.

The trade routeThe degree route
Pathtrade → foreman → superintendentdegree → assistant PM → project manager
Where it lands⚠ often self-employed contracting⚠ employment by a large firm
Florida licence timeline4 years, incl. 1 as foreman✅ 1 year, on the degree
Earnings shapewhatever the business makesa salary with a ceiling and a floor

⚠ Neither is better and they are genuinely different careers. The trade route builds equity in a business and carries its risk; the degree route buys a salary and a title at a firm. What you should not do is drift into one while believing you are on the other, which is what happens when someone takes a construction degree expecting to end up running their own crew, or spends eight years on site expecting a corporate project-management job to appear.

What the work actually is

O*NET, on construction managers: inspect or review projects to monitor compliance with building and safety codes or other regulations; plan, schedule, or coordinate construction project activities to meet deadlines; direct and supervise construction or related workers; prepare and submit budget estimates, progress reports, or cost tracking reports; confer with supervisory personnel, owners, contractors, or design professionals to discuss and resolve matters.

⚠⚠ Every one of those is about other people's work. A construction manager builds nothing personally and is accountable for everything. The skill is sequencing, negotiating and forecasting — and absorbing the fact that weather, a late delivery and a subcontractor's cashflow are all now your problem.

✅ O*NET and the BLS agree: O*NET gives 550,300 employed, much faster than average (7% or higher) on 2024–34 and 46,800 annual openings; the BLS gives 609,100 jobs, 9% growth on 2025–35 and +55,200. At $114,990 this is the best-paid non-engineering, non-medical path on this site.

⚠⚠⚠ Florida files this somewhere unexpected

If you search Florida for a “construction management” degree by its federal code you will find nothing — no Florida public institution awards under it. The state teaches the subject as construction engineering technology: 16 public institutions, 521 credentials, 305 of them bachelor's degrees, with a master's tier above and associate and certificate routes below. UF 128, FIU 120, Seminole State 71, UNF 58, Valencia 40.

⚠ That placement is a hint about the degree's character. It sits with engineering technology, not with business — statics, materials, mechanical and electrical systems, drawings. Expect more technical content than a management degree implies, and note the practical consequence below.

⚠⚠ The degree is worth three years of your life, in writing

Florida's contractor statute is unusually explicit about what a degree is worth. Section 489.111(2)(c) accepts:

  • a baccalaureate in engineering, architecture or building construction plus one year of proven experience; or
  • four years of active experience in the trade, at least one as a foreman; or
  • intermediate combinations trading college credits against foreman years.

⚠⚠⚠ So the degree replaces three of the four years. On a full-time basis — the statute counts 2,000 person-hours as a year — that is three years of earnings and three years of life, which is a far more concrete return than most degrees can point to.

⚠ But read the field list. The pathway names engineering, architecture or building construction. A business administration degree is perfectly acceptable to an employer hiring a construction manager and does not satisfy this route — so if a licence is anywhere in your plan, the degree subject matters more than the degree.

⚠ The course numbers do not travel well

Florida carries 334 building construction course numbers across 26 public institutions, and the most widely shared reaches only 9 — about 35%. Compare that with accounting's 97% or economics' 100%. The recognisable spine is thin: BCN 2405 Applied Statics and Strength (9), BCN 1272 Plans Interpretation (8), BCN 1251C Building Construction Drawing (8), BCN 1001 Introduction to Building Construction (7).

⚠⚠ Treat these as one-institution programmes. Take the general education and the mathematics anywhere; take the construction sequence in one place, and if you must move, expect the receiving department to evaluate you course by course rather than by number.

Necessary skills

  • Reading drawings fluently, and spotting what is missing from them before it is built wrong.
  • Estimating and scheduling. The two quantitative skills the job is judged on, and the ones that decide whether a project makes money.
  • Contract literacy. Change orders, retainage, liens and delay claims are where projects are won and lost financially.
  • Safety, meant rather than documented. Construction remains among the most dangerous industries, and the manager owns it.
  • Negotiating with people who do not report to you — subcontractors, inspectors, owners and designers.
  • Composure when the schedule breaks, which it will, and calmly rebuilding the sequence around it.

Advice

⚠⚠ Decide early whether you want a salary or a business, because it changes the degree. If it is a firm job, a construction or business degree plus internships is the route. If it is your own licence and your own crew, take the construction or engineering degree specifically — it converts to three years of the licence requirement, and business does not.

⚠ Get on a site while studying. This is the path on this site where summer work is most directly convertible: it counts toward the experience requirement, it teaches you what the drawings mean, and it is how the firms recruit.

⚠ Do not aim at cost estimating as a destination. It pays reasonably at $78,740 but it is the one role in this family projected to shrink, by 6,900 jobs over the decade. Estimating is an excellent skill and a narrowing job title — learn it inside a management role.

And take the statics and materials courses seriously. Florida teaches this as engineering technology for a reason: the manager who can tell whether a subcontractor's objection is real is worth much more than one who has to ask.

cipCodes.note: Construction engineering technology — ⚠ where Florida ACTUALLY files construction management: 16 public institutions and 521 credentials, against ZERO Florida public institutions on the federal Construction Management code that this path is nominally anchored to.

Civil engineering — a genuine feeder and the design side of the same projects. ⚠ It also satisfies Florida's contractor-licence education route under s. 489.111, which names engineering explicitly, so it keeps both the design and the contracting doors open.

⚠ Business administration — accepted by employers hiring construction managers, since the federal handbook names business as a suitable degree field. ⚠⚠ But it does NOT satisfy Florida's contractor-licence education pathway, which names engineering, architecture and building construction only.

Building and construction trades and site management — the trade route. Included because it is how roughly half the people supervising Florida construction sites actually got there, and because Florida credits trade experience directly toward a contractor licence.

programs.note: The programme itself — 16 Florida public institutions, taught as construction engineering technology rather than as a business subject. ⚠ Read its degrees note: the degree substitutes for three years of site experience toward a Florida contractor licence, which is the strongest financial argument for taking it.

⚠ A real route, and the harder one: civil engineering designs what construction management delivers, leads toward the PE licence, and equally satisfies Florida's contractor-licence education pathway. ⚠⚠ Easier to move from civil engineering into construction management than the reverse, so it is the more open choice if you can carry the mathematics.
⚠ The closest sibling, often the same department. The practical test of which you are looking at: whether the capstone is a design problem or a bid and a schedule.

⚠⚠ Accepted by employers and NOT accepted by the licensing statute — the single most useful distinction on this page. A business degree can make you a construction manager at a firm; it leaves you on the four-year experience route to your own contractor licence.

courses.reason: Introduction to Building Construction — 7 institutions. The industry, its contracts and delivery methods, and the vocabulary the rest of the programme assumes.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ The building construction prefix is fragmented: 334 numbers across 26 institutions with the most shared reaching only 9. Expect your college's sequence to use different numbers from any other's.

courses.reason: Plans Interpretation — 8 institutions. Reading construction drawings and specifications, which is the literacy the entire job rests on.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Closely related to BCN1251C Building Construction Drawing (8 institutions), and some colleges combine them. Check which your programme requires.

courses.reason: Building Construction Drawing — 8 institutions. Producing and marking up drawings rather than only reading them, usually with CAD.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also carried as BCN1251 without the integrated lab at 4 institutions.

courses.reason: Applied Statics and Strength of Materials — 9 institutions, the most widely carried course in the prefix. ⚠ The reason Florida files this degree under engineering technology: forces, loads and why structures stand up.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ The course most likely to surprise someone who chose construction management expecting a business degree. It is also what lets a manager judge whether a subcontractor's objection is real.

courses.reason: Construction Materials — 4 institutions. Concrete, steel, timber and masonry: properties, testing and what fails in Florida's climate.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also carried as BCN1210 (4 institutions) and BCN2230 Construction Materials and Methods (4). Three numbers, one subject.

courses.reason: Mechanical and Electrical Systems — 5 institutions. The building services that consume a large share of the budget and cause a large share of the coordination problems.
Construction Planning and Cost Control — 4 institutions. Scheduling and cost management, which is what the job is actually judged on.
Construction Safety — 4 institutions. ⚠ Construction remains among the most dangerous industries and the manager owns site safety. This is also where OSHA training usually sits.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Ask whether the course includes the OSHA 30-hour card. Many employers expect it and some will not let you on site without the 10-hour at minimum.

courses.reason: Construction Estimating II — 4 institutions. Quantity take-off and bid preparation: the skill that decides whether work is won and whether it is won profitably.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Cost estimating as a JOB TITLE is projected to decline 3%, but the skill is core to construction management. Learn it; do not specialise into it.

courses.reason: Project Case Study — 4 institutions. The capstone: a real project taken from documents to bid and schedule, and the closest thing in the degree to the job.
Calculus for Business and Social Science — 36 institutions. The mathematics most construction management degrees require, and the one that travels from any Florida state college.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ If the programme sits in an engineering college, check whether it wants MAC2311 Calculus I (39 institutions) instead — construction engineering technology programmes sometimes do.

courses.reason: Financial Accounting — 32 institutions. Job costing, cashflow and retainage are accounting problems, and a manager who cannot read a project's financials cannot control it.
Business Law I — 25 institutions. Contracts, change orders, liens and delay claims are where construction projects are won and lost financially.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Where your programme offers a dedicated construction law or contracts course, take that as well — it is the most directly applicable law a construction manager uses.

courses.reason: Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Estimating, productivity measurement and risk allowances all rest on it.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. Requests for information, change-order justifications and delay notices are written documents that end up in disputes.
